description: WebGPU inference framework layer — src/main.ts with adapter + device + compute pipeline driving a real matmul WGSL kernel, plus the matmul shader itself.

buildHints.whenToUse: Any product that needs to run ML inference inside the browser tab with GPU acceleration — small transformers, embeddings, classifiers, or custom WGSL compute kernels. Pick this over server inference when the workload is latency-sensitive, privacy-sensitive, or must work offline.
firstSteps: Install: `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173. Open Chrome 113+, Edge 113+, or Safari 18+; the page prints the output matrix from a GPU matmul.
The compute pipeline lives in `src/main.ts` — adapter → device → buffers → bind group → pipeline → dispatch → readback. It runs a 4x4 @ 4x4 matmul end-to-end on the GPU.
The WGSL kernel is in `src/shaders/matmul.wgsl` — edit the workgroup size, tiling, or the inner dot product to benchmark different strategies against a CPU reference.
For production ML, uncomment the Transformers.js path in `src/main.ts` and `pnpm add @huggingface/transformers` — it auto-detects WebGPU and runs ONNX models with a single `pipeline()` call.
Build: `pnpm build` emits static assets to `dist/` — deploy to any static host. WebGPU requires HTTPS in production (localhost is exempt).
gotchas: WebGPU is Chrome/Edge 113+ and Safari 18+ stable. Firefox ships it behind `dom.webgpu.enabled` — always feature-detect `navigator.gpu` and fall back to WebAssembly SIMD (Transformers.js does this automatically).
`requestAdapter()` returns `null` on iGPU-blocklisted devices and in private/incognito on some platforms — do not assume adapter is non-null. Surface a user-visible fallback message.

Buffer sizes must be multiples of 4 bytes and declared with the right `usage` flags — STORAGE for shader-writable, COPY_SRC to read back via a staging buffer, COPY_DST to upload input. Missing COPY_SRC silently produces zeros on readback.
`mapAsync(GPUMapMode.READ)` requires a buffer created with MAP_READ | COPY_DST — you cannot map a STORAGE buffer directly. Always copy STORAGE → staging → map.

Workgroup size in the WGSL (`@workgroup_size(x,y,z)`) must match the `dispatchWorkgroups(a,b,c)` call such that `a*x`, `b*y`, `c*z` cover the output tensor dimensions. Off-by-one here produces partial outputs with zero-filled tails.
Shader compilation errors are async — call `await shaderModule.getCompilationInfo()` and check `.messages` during development; a broken shader otherwise produces silent NaN outputs.
architectureNotes: Create one GPUDevice per page and reuse it across inference calls — `requestDevice()` is expensive and each device has its own command queue and buffer pool.
Keep bind group layouts explicit (not auto-generated) once the model stabilizes — auto layouts regenerate on each pipeline creation and fragment the cache, hurting cold-start latency.
For multi-kernel pipelines (attention + MLP + layernorm), batch commands into a single GPUCommandEncoder before submitting — each `queue.submit` incurs a kernel-launch roundtrip.

placeholders.description: WebGPU bootstrap — adapter, device, input/output/staging buffers, bind group, compute pipeline, dispatch, readback, DOM print. Replace the 4x4 matmul with the product's real kernel (attention QK^T, GEMM, convolution) or flip to the Transformers.js branch for ONNX models.
Minimal tiled matmul compute shader. Extend for fused kernels (matmul + bias + activation), different dtypes (f16 via the shader-f16 feature), or quantization (int8 dot-product via DP4a).
